K1.title: A1: small repeated models drawn brown and see-through (repro on HEAD, then fix)
K1.evidence: Reproduced by GameDeveloperSkill (KayKit tree_single_A.gltf x200 brown and see-through; trees_A_medium.gltf with the same texture correct; NC_INSTANCING=0 fixes it). Ruled out by reading the code: the class key has textures, every material parameter, fade/fadeInvert, alpha mode, every vertex and index stream (glmodern_scene.inc:473-523, glmodern.cpp:5561); a 95-vertex tree has no LOD (lodMinTriangles = 256, cooker.h:29), so no LOD cross-fade.
files: engine/src/renderer/pipeline/glmodern.cpp (forwardPipeline, uploadItems ~5558, GPU-driven draws after the CPU forward ~10577)
steps: Reproduce on HEAD with the KayKit level (or 200 copies of any < 256-triangle textured glTF next to a bigger one sharing its texture). Run in this order and keep the screenshots: default; NC_GPU_DRIVEN=0 with instancing on (picture fixed -> the GPU-driven path; still wrong -> the instance classes or the instanced shader variant); NC_EDITOR_VIEWMODE=basecolor (one flat colour = one texel of the atlas sampled: UV stream); NC_INSTANCING=0 (control).

Check the two .gltf files: attributes, COLOR_0, texCoord index of baseColorTexture, alphaMode/alphaCutoff. A model without COLOR_0 next to one with it, or texCoord 1, is the first suspect for a variant-dependent stream bind.

Candidate 1: the UV/colour stream of the instanced or GPU-driven variant (gdBindStreams binds slot 2 only when it.variant & 2, gdRecordGbufClass when shade.uv(); compare with the streams forwardPipeline expects for the same material). A missing UV bind reads UV 0 = one texel = uniform brown; the see-through look is fragments discarded by ncCoverage with that texel's alpha.

Candidate 2: an object-wide crossFade stuck below 1 (streaming fade-in or HLOD fade, glscenemodel.cpp ~5535) on items that then enter the GPU-driven class with fade < 1 forever. Log crossFade of the items of the wrong class for a frame.
Fix at the root, add a regression scene to tests/smoke (two models of different vertex formats sharing a texture, 200 copies, screenshot compared against NC_INSTANCING=0 with tests/cook/pngdiff.py).
acceptance: the default picture equals the NC_INSTANCING=0 picture (pngdiff under the threshold) on OpenGL, D3D12 and Vulkan
GameDeveloperSkill bench H8: 'gpu-driven-off vs base picture difference %' and 'instancing-off vs base' both < 1 %
no change in GPU ms of the forest bench (tests/bench/perf/gpu_driven.sh)

H1.title: Texture mip streaming without CPU pixel copies (Megascans close-up drops)
steps: Profile one approach hitch (NC_PROFILE_REPORT slow frames): which zone, how many MB uploaded that frame.

makeSrgbCopy: an uncompressed colour texture without mip levels, or on a device without Caps::srgbViewsRgba8, is read back from the GPU (a full stall) on its first draw and again after every restream to another size. Create sRGB textures with an sRGB format at upload (as UE does) or with an sRGB view always; never read back on the render thread.
Plan N2 of CLAUDE.md: mips read from the DDS straight into an upload heap ring (no CPU pixel copy, no RGBA conversion), copy queue on D3D12, a fence per mip; budget per frame in MB, not in textures.
Upload coarse mips first and keep them resident; fine mips by screen-space texel density (UE's mip bias by distance), with hysteresis so walking back does not evict and reload.
Keep NC_TEXTURE_STREAM_V2=0 for the old path.
acceptance: bench H1 'approach' hitches -80 % or more against base, p99 under 2x p50
no visible blur longer than 0.5 s at 2 m (screenshot after 0.5 s equals the warm one)
H1.prompt: In the NucleonEngine repository (follow CLAUDE.md), branch perf/texture-mip-streaming: the GameDeveloperSkill bench confirmed that walking up to Megascans assets hitches on texture mip uploads ({evidence}). Implement N2: DDS mips straight into an upload ring without CPU pixel copies, the copy queue on D3D12, a per-frame MB budget, coarse mips resident first, fine mips by texel density with hysteresis; NC_TEXTURE_STREAM_V2=0 keeps the old path. Done when the bench H1 approach scenario loses 80 % of its hitches on the same GPU. Verify with windows.ps1 -Changed.

H2.title: Virtual geometry page streaming: pool size, prefetch and load budget
steps: Pool size from the VRAM budget (default a fraction of it, not a fixed 64 MB), NC_VIRTUAL_POOL_MB overrides.
Prefetch by distance and camera velocity (pages of the next LOD level before they are needed), as Nanite's streaming priority.
Read pages from the pak with the IO scheduler (no temp file), decode on workers, upload in a budget measured in ms.
Never stall the frame on a page: draw the coarser resident cluster.
acceptance: bench H2 approach/fly hitches -70 % against base
poolUsedMB stays under the new budget, no frame waits on pages
H2.prompt: In the NucleonEngine repository (follow CLAUDE.md), branch perf/vgeo-streaming: the GameDeveloperSkill bench confirmed that the close-up drops of virtualized assets come from geometry page streaming ({evidence}). Size the page pool from the VRAM budget, prefetch pages by distance and camera speed, read them from the pak through the IO scheduler without temp files, decode on workers, upload within a ms budget, and never stall: draw the coarser resident clusters. Keep a switch to the old behaviour. Done when bench H2 loses 70 % of its hitches.

H4.title: Shadows: per-cascade culling, cached cascades, LOD and no wind in far casters
steps: Cull casters (and terrain chunks) per cascade frustum, not once for all cascades.
Casters use a coarser LOD than the view (LOD bias per cascade), no wind beyond NC_SHADOW_WIND_DISTANCE by default.
Cache the far cascades and redraw them only when the sun or the static set changes (UE's cached shadow maps / VSM page caching).
Impostor shadows beyond the impostor distance.
acceptance: bench H4 shadow passes under 25 % of the GPU frame, view p50 -20 % on the forest
screenshots of the shadows unchanged within the threshold near the camera

Done when shadow passes are under 25 % of the GPU frame and the view p50 drops 20 %.

H5.title: LOD policy: screen-size thresholds and LOD chains for every repeated asset
steps: Switch LOD by projected screen size (UE's screen size), not distance only, with a per-project bias in the scalability groups.
Generate LODs for repeated assets even under lodMinTriangles when the instance count is high (the cost is count x triangles).
GPU LOD (NC_GPU_LOD) on by default once it matches the CPU choice.
acceptance: bench H5: base within 10 % of lod-coarsest on the far views, no popping visible at the switch distance (dither cross-fade)
